generator.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: transparent original Capydoku 2D skeletal animation limb sprite atlas.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: our own eight-part 4-column by 2-row transparent atlas. Preserve its exact canvas, grid, scale, location, orientation, warm golden palette, hand-drawn outline style, and transparent alpha background.
CHANGE ONLY the attachment-cap artwork on the FOUR GOLDEN ARM SEGMENTS in columns 1 and 2, both rows. Each segment must remain a complete solid isolated piece. At the upper/proximal end, which overlaps its connected arm segment, remove the separate crescent rim/highlight and ring-shaped shadow; fill smoothly with the same mid-tone golden fur color as the neighboring shaft. At the lower/distal end also remove the terminal crescent/ring shading so rotated overlapping pieces do not look like two stacked elbow cuffs. Keep gentle shaft shading in the central 60%; let attachment zones at both ends be low-contrast flat warm gold with NO dark transverse cap outline and NO end-ring. Slightly taper the attachment ends inward only if needed to eliminate the bulbous cap, maintaining full solid overlap coverage. Preserve the established dark long-side outer contour and small fur tufts on the shaft, but fade any long-side line out before it crosses an attachment end.
DO NOT change the two brown paws and two brown feet in columns 3 and 4, any pixels outside these four golden arm pieces, or add/change any objects. No new face, head, body, eyes, mouths, poses, joints, labels, panels, background color, grid lines, watermark, or shadows outside the sprites. Do not render a combined character. Do not add holes, masks, opaque backdrop, detached patches, or translucent parts. The output must remain the same eight-part atlas on a genuinely transparent background. This is a very localized cleanup, not a redesign.

findings.elbowCaps: Compared final 0.2.29 and targeted 0.2.30 250pt cheer captures directly. The conspicuous terminal crescent shading/highlight around each elbow is reduced; there is no new dark transverse cap seam. Complete arm overlap is visible at all three sizes. The joint silhouette remains visibly built from overlapping rounded parts on close inspection, so this is an improvement rather than a seamless-mesh claim.
findings.mouthAttachment: All three current-rig mouth captures place the three dots beside the lower snout/right mouth corner, visibly below the nostril rather than near it. All three fallback captures do likewise using the original complete-character image. The marked-mouth relationship and inheritance through nod are additionally checked by the passing actual presentation-layer test.
findings.bounds: All 15 captures show complete feet/head/paws and visible outer margin; no visible clipped dot or disconnected limb. The unchanged part bounds assertions and new mouth-bubble bounds assertions passed in r2.
findings.starGrip: Both paws remain in front of the held star in the three hugging captures; the star still partly covers the left cheek as in the prior design. No new overlap/z-order defect observed.
findings.expressionAndDepth: Happy and sad heads retain the original expression/art style. Shoulder roots remain behind torso/head; forearms and paws retain the intended overlap. Eyes/mouth have not been redesigned or animated. Complete-image fallback is deliberately a different old full-body pose, not asserted identical to the normal rig.

observations.finding: Arms progress from the lowered anticipation through raised cheer to a stable raised terminal pose. End-cap shading remains softer through sampled elbow bends. Full paws remain within decoration; no obvious detached arm, duplicate silhouette or switch to legacy full art in the sampled sequence.
Both paws track the star during lift, hold and settling. The star remains in front of the face/hands arrangement as authored; no hand/prop detachment or terminal image replacement observed.

Head bows and returns with arm movement. At requested 7.0s (actual 6.9966667s) the three sigh dots appear beside the mouth; at 7.2s they remain beside the moving mouth, then disappear while the same sad rig settles. No observed dot emerging at the nostril.

limits: This is a simulator test-host recording, not ordinary application navigation or physical-device gameplay.
The configured host holds each performance for about 1.4s; labeled frame ranges are sampled observation intervals, not exact measured animation durations.
Sampling every 0.2s cannot establish per-frame continuity, FPS, device input/audio/haptic feel or absence of every short transient artifact.
Art remains a cutout rig with fixed happy/sad head textures; no claim of Meowdoku aesthetic equivalence.
